Use this page if your study needs medication given in hospital, which is not in
the prescription register LMDB (see [Medication (ATC)](medication.qmd#coverage)).
Cancer drugs and biologics given at a hospital are typical examples. SMR is not
a DST register. It is held by the Danish Health Data Authority
(Sundhedsdatastyrelsen, SDS), its data quality has not yet been evaluated, and
some clinical specialties are missing ([Rosenkrantz et al.
2024](https://doi.org/10.2147/CLEP.S487838)). This page says what to check
before you rely on it.

## What SMR holds {#what-smr-holds}

The Hospital Medication Register (Sygehusmedicinregisteret, SMR) holds
medication given or dispensed at public hospitals and hospital outpatient
clinics, reported by the five regions. The regions started reporting on 15 May
2018, so there is nothing before that date ([data declaration, June
2026](https://cdn1.gopublic.dk/sundhedsdatastyrelsen/Media/639178923683784980/datadeklaration-smr-v2-juni-2026.pdf),
section 1.2).
Private hospitals, hospices and specialist hospitals run as independent
institutions are not reported
([data declaration, June 2026](https://cdn1.gopublic.dk/sundhedsdatastyrelsen/Media/639178923683784980/datadeklaration-smr-v2-juni-2026.pdf)).

You apply for SMR through the Forskerservice of SDS, which says that data are
as a rule made available on research machines at SDS or at DST
([Forskerservice](https://sundhedsdatastyrelsen.dk/data-og-registre/forskerservice)).
Ask Forskerservice how SMR will reach your project before you plan the linkage
to your DST registers. SDS also warns that replacement civil registration (CPR)
numbers are not unique across regions, so read `V_CPR` together with the region
([data declaration, section 4.1.16](https://cdn1.gopublic.dk/sundhedsdatastyrelsen/Media/639178923683784980/datadeklaration-smr-v2-juni-2026.pdf)).

The column names below are the ones in SDS's data declaration. Check them
against the columns in your own delivery with `colnames()`.

## Completeness differs by region and drug {#completeness}

At the end of 2022 SDS wrote that heavy medicines (cancer drugs and biologics)
were missing for Region Nordjylland and Region Syddanmark. Dispensed medicine
was missing for Region Hovedstaden, Region Sjælland, Region Nordjylland and
Region Syddanmark, and only partly reported by Region Midtjylland. A cost could
be calculated for only about 60% of the reported administrations
([SDS, gevinstrealisering i forbindelse med SMR2-projektet, 9 March
2023](https://cdn1.gopublic.dk/sundhedsdatastyrelsen/Media/639120159392949453/gevinstrealisering-i-forbindelse-med-smr2-projektet.pdf)).

The June 2026 declaration describes cancer drugs region by region:

- **Midtjylland** reports them from early 2019 for oncology departments, from
  September 2019 for haematology outpatients, from mid-2021 for haematology
  inpatients and from early 2023 for children and young people.
- **Nordjylland** does not give parenteral cancer drugs in the medication
  module, so they are not reported. Reporting from the haematology department
  starts in August 2025.
- **Syddanmark** does not handle cancer drugs in the medication module. An
  electronic treatment scheme was in use in some departments in September 2025,
  and SDS calls the data incomplete.
- **Hovedstaden and Sjælland** do not report cytostatics dispensed for home
  treatment.

A zero count for a cancer drug or a biologic in a region is therefore not
evidence of no use. The same section lists other gaps, such as intensive care
and anaesthesia, eye departments and some outpatient clinics. Read the entries
for the departments and drugs in your study.

## Breaks when a region moves to reporting guide 2.0 {#guide-2}

Each region moves from reporting guide 1.x to reporting guide 2.0 (called
"SMR2" in the declaration) on its own date. Rows from before and after the move
are not the same kind of rows.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Guide 2.0 dates, mixtures and infusion times by region"}
| Region                | Guide 2.0 from             | Mixtures                                                                    | Infusion time in `D_ADM` before 2.0                              |
| --------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Nordjylland           | April 2025                 | One row per administration from March 2022, no dose for the components      | Take-down time, from April 2022 (end date not given)             |
| Midtjylland           | October 2025               | A main row plus one row per component from February 2021, no component dose | Start time, but the row is reported at take-down, from June 2019 |
| Syddanmark            | September 2025             | Not registered in the medication module                                     | Take-down time until autumn 2023, start time after               |
| Hovedstaden, Sjælland | No date in the declaration | Not split into components                                                   | Start time chosen by the user                                    |
:::

What changes in your data at the move
([data declaration, sections 2.4 and 4.1](https://cdn1.gopublic.dk/sundhedsdatastyrelsen/Media/639178923683784980/datadeklaration-smr-v2-juni-2026.pdf)):

- **Rows that disappear.** Guide 2.0 does not allow dose 0 (an administration
  that was planned but not given), future administrations or the patient's own
  medicine. Nordjylland, Midtjylland and Syddanmark reported dose 0 before the
  move, Midtjylland reported dispensed medicine as administrations dated in the
  future from February 2021, and Nordjylland reported own medicine from May
  2018. Earlier periods therefore contain rows that later periods do not.
  Dropping rows with `V_ADM_DOSIS` 0 in every period removes the first of
  these differences, but not the other two. In one project's delivery from
  June 2026, Hovedstaden and Sjælland also had rows with dose 0, and
  Syddanmark still had them after September 2025, so count them per region
  and month in your own delivery rather than relying on the dates above.
- **A new administration key.** Under 2.0 `K_ADM_ID` is a new synthetic key.
  SDS writes that it "Er ikke kompatibel, med nøglen i version 1.x." Do not use
  it to link rows reported before and after a region's move.
- **Deleted rows.** A row that was reported and later deleted in the hospital
  system stays in SMR with `C_SLETTET = 1`. Rows that are not deleted have
  `C_SLETTET = 0`. If your delivery has the column, remove the deleted rows.
- **Dose units.** Before 2.0 each region used its own unit list. In
  Hovedstaden and Sjælland the unit can be a rate or a concentration, such as
  mg/kg, mg/ml or microgram/kg/min, instead of an amount. Check the units in
  `V_ADM_DOSIS_ENHED` before you sum doses.
- **Infusions.** The table above shows which time `D_ADM` holds for a
  continuous infusion. An infusion reported at take-down can fall in a later
  month than it started.

## ATC codes change over time {#atc-changes}

`C_ATC` is the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) code that was valid when
the drug was given ([data declaration, section
4.1.22](https://cdn1.gopublic.dk/sundhedsdatastyrelsen/Media/639178923683784980/datadeklaration-smr-v2-juni-2026.pdf)),
and WHO revises the ATC system every year. A drug can therefore have one code
early in the register and another later. The monoclonal antibodies are an
example: they were under `L01XC` and are now under `L01F` in [WHO's ATC
index](https://atcddd.fhi.no/atc_ddd_index/?code=L01F). A filter on the old
code alone loses the later rows, and the drop looks like a break in the
register. Look up whether the drugs in your study changed code during your
study period, and filter on both the old and the new code.

## Check your drugs before you use them {#check}

Plot the number of administrations per region and month for the drugs in your
study, as the [LPR page](understand-lpr.qmd#lpr3-spike) does for the change in
diagnoses around 2019-2020. A region where a drug is absent, or where the
count jumps at a move to guide 2.0, tells you where the register cannot answer
your question. The sketch below uses the declaration's column names in lower
case and the monoclonal antibodies as the example, under both their old and
their new ATC code. `smr` is your opened SMR table, opened in the same way as
`lmdb` in [Extract the dispensings](medication.qmd#the-pattern): `read_register()`
with your SMR table's name, then `rename_with(tolower)`. fastreg 0.14.1, the
version on CRAN, converts a file with no year in its name, such as a single SMR
file, into a folder that its `read_register()` does not look for. Open it with
`read_parquet_dataset()` and the full path instead, as in [When
`read_register()` cannot find the
register](parquet-and-fastreg.qmd#when-read-register-fails). The version of
fastreg on GitHub finds it.

```r
library(dplyr)   # rename_with, filter, select, collect, mutate, count
library(ggplot2) # ggplot, geom_col, facet_wrap

smr_counts <- smr %>%
  rename_with(tolower) %>%
  filter(grepl("^L01XC|^L01F", c_atc)) %>%    # monoclonal antibodies: old code L01XC, current code L01F
  select(k_region_id, d_adm, c_slettet) %>%   # no c_slettet in your delivery: drop it here
  collect() %>%
  filter(c_slettet == 0) %>%                  # ... and drop this line
  mutate(month = as.Date(format(as.Date(d_adm), "%Y-%m-01"))) %>%
  count(k_region_id, month)                   # administrations per region and month

ggplot(smr_counts, aes(x = month, y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~ k_region_id, scales = "free_y") # one panel per region
```

A figure that leaves the research machine must be aggregated, as in [Figures
for publication](figures.qmd). Months with few administrations are small cells,
see [Export](export.qmd).
